QF.id: XC Investment Products and Market Developments_9

question.text: Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) in India must distribute what percentage of their net distributable cash flows to unit holders?

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the SEBI (Infrastructure Investment Trusts) Regulations, an InvIT is required to distribute at least 90% of its net distributable cash flows to unit holders on the prescribed periodic basis. The high payout ratio is what gives InvITs their income-oriented profile. The Trap: 50% and 75% understate the mandated minimum payout. 100% is not required either — the regulation sets a floor of 90%, leaving a small portion for working-capital needs. Note: The NISM Series X-A Investment Adviser (Level 1) workbook discusses InvITs as a product category, but the specific 90% net-distributable-cash-flow distribution requirement was not located in the X-A or Series IX workbook pages reviewed (note that a separate 90% figure appears for Infrastructure Debt Schemes' portfolio composition, which is a different rule). The framing above is presented as general SEBI InvIT-regulation industry knowledge rather than a workbook citation.
